lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project wetland herbs through a persistent perigynous floral tube/hypanthium surrounding a usually superior ovary, then split Ammannia, Lythrum and Rotala by leaf-base and inflorescence/flower architecture.

project_scope.selection_mode: Project module across Ammannia, Lythrum and Rotala
project_scope.note: Five source taxa are represented: Ammannia coccinea, A. auriculata, Lythrum alatum, L. californicum and Rotala ramosior. Current Kew/FNA treatments retain these species concepts.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Inspect one flower from the side. The sepals form a persistent tubular or cup-shaped floral tube/hypanthium; petals arise near its rim, while the ovary in the project genera is superior and sits inside rather than being fused below the flower.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly wetland or amphibious herbs in the project pool. Leaves simple and entire, commonly opposite, sometimes shifting toward alternate or whorled arrangements.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and 4–6-merous. Petals may be obvious, tiny, caducous or absent; stamens are inserted on the floral tube. Heterostyly occurs in Lythrum and elsewhere in the family.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a many-seeded capsule, often partly enclosed by the persistent floral tube; dehiscence may be valvate, septicidal, septifragal or irregular depending genus.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: The durable family door is persistent perigynous floral tube + usually superior ovary + many-seeded capsule, not purple flower color.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: floral tube/hypanthium → superior ovary relationship → capsule → genus doors → Onagraceae/Myrtaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Lythraceae is easiest once the learner sees that the cup around the ovary is floral tube, not an inferior ovary. That single side-view comparison separates it cleanly from close Myrtales relatives.

steps.title: 1 · Find the persistent floral tube
steps.look_for: A ribbed or smooth cup/tube surrounding the ovary, with sepals at the rim and petals attached near the rim.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the central family architecture shared by the project genera.

steps.title: 2 · Show that the ovary is superior
steps.photo_role: flower cutaway or labeled side view
steps.look_for: The ovary sits free inside the floral tube rather than being fused below the other flower parts.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest Lythraceae-vs-Onagraceae/Myrtaceae tie-breaker in the project.

steps.title: 3 · Ammannia door
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves; in the flora area leaf bases often auriculate; small axillary cymes and a ribbed floral tube; capsule splits irregularly.
steps.why_it_matters: Auriculate leaf bases are especially useful against Rotala ramosior.

steps.title: 4 · Lythrum door
steps.look_for: More obvious racemose purple flowers with a cylindrical floral tube; project species have 6 stamens and native North American Lythrum are distylous.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the loosestrife architecture distinct from the tiny toothcup-type genera.

steps.title: 5 · Rotala door
steps.photo_role: Rotala ramosior node + tiny axillary flower
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves with tapered—not auriculate—bases and tiny solitary axillary flowers; petals are often absent or minute.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest project split from Ammannia.

steps.title: 6 · Follow the flower to capsule
steps.look_for: A dry many-seeded capsule remaining partly surrounded by the old floral tube.
steps.why_it_matters: Reinforces the family architecture after petals are gone.

comparisons.title: Lythraceae vs Onagraceae
comparisons.rule: Project Lythraceae usually has a superior ovary sitting inside a perigynous floral tube; Onagraceae has an inferior ovary below the floral tube/hypanthium.

comparisons.title: Lythraceae vs Myrtaceae
comparisons.rule: Lythraceae project plants are wetland herbs with a floral tube, relatively few-to-moderate stamens and usually superior ovary; Myrtaceae project plant is woody with pellucid oil glands, an intramarginal vein, many stamens and an inferior ovary.

comparisons.title: Ammannia vs Rotala
comparisons.rule: In the FNA flora area, Ammannia commonly has auriculate leaf bases; Rotala ramosior has tapered leaf bases and tiny solitary axillary flowers.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not make petal presence, leaf arrangement or one capsule-opening pattern absolute. Those characters vary within Lythraceae; the floral-tube/ovary relationship is more transferable.
